content:
Whitney's reference is a short blurb that names HighLevel, says the system is customized for the wedding industry, and lists its features: pipelines, automated text and email responses, follow-up workflows, and online scheduling. Her framing is "from manually chasing every inquiry to nurturing leads on autopilot."

Candidate A is short and in the right register. But it leaves out HighLevel and the industry customization, and it names few specific features (no pipelines, no text and email detail). "Turns inquiries into 'yes'" is a bit cutesy, and the "no more missed messages" claims are absolute. It would need some additions.

Candidate B is longer. It includes HighLevel, the industry-specific strategy, the pipeline tracking, the text and email responses, and the scheduling. It also keeps the substance of Daniela's draft, which Whitney had said "Yes!" to. It runs three paragraphs, which is longer than the reference, and it might need trimming for a form field. "Tours" is a good venue-specific touch. Its content is accurate and complete.

Substance favors B, since it covers what Whitney kept. Length favors A, but A is missing key elements. A would need a few additions, while B would need trimming.

{"winner": "B", "edits_needed_A": "some", "edits_needed_B": "few", "reason": "B keeps the substance Whitney's version includes (HighLevel, wedding-industry customization, pipelines, text/email responses, follow-up, scheduling) and only needs trimming for length. A is punchy but omits HighLevel and the industry customization, and its 'yes' tagline and absolute claims need reworking."}

request.system:
You compare two draft pieces of marketing copy for Wedding Industry Ads (WIA), a wedding-industry advertising agency. You are given the request, the version WIA's co-founder Whitney actually approved or wrote (the reference), and two candidate drafts. Decide which candidate would need fewer and smaller edits to become something Whitney would approve. Judge substance first (what is claimed, for whom, how WIA is positioned, accuracy, whether her own wording was kept where she supplied it), then voice. Do not reward length, and do not require the candidate to copy the reference wording.

Return only JSON: {"winner": "A" or "B" or "tie", "edits_needed_A": "few", "edits_needed_B": "many", "reason": "one or two sentences"} where edits_needed values are none, few, some or many.
request.user:
Request:
LeadLock is sponsoring a conference for venues next month. We need to fill out a sponsor form. One of the questions is "Blurb about your company and what it does". This is what Daniela drafted below. Give me your thoughts. Positive and negative.

LeadLock is a lead management system designed to help wedding pros and venues convert more inquiries into booked appointments.

Streamline your inquiry process, automate follow-up, and convert more leads into booked clients. Built on the HighLevel platform and powered by our industry-specific strategy, templates, and workflows, LeadLock fills the critical gap between marketing and sales. From instant text and email responses to fully automated nurture sequences, pipeline tracking, and appointment scheduling, LeadLock ensures no lead ever slips through the cracks - so business owners can book more clients with less stress.

We help small business owners organize their leads, respond instantly, eliminate follow-up bottlenecks, and finally stop losing opportunities due to slow response times or disorganized inboxes - so they can focus on delivering an exceptional client experience.


Yes!

Reference (what Whitney approved):
LeadLock gives venues and wedding professionals a powerful lead management system. Built on HighLevel and customized for the wedding industry, LeadLock helps you go from manually chasing every inquiry to nurturing leads on autopilot. With organized pipelines, automated text & email inquiry responses, smart follow-up workflows,  and easy online consultation schedule, you'll convert more clients with ease.

Candidate A:
**LeadLock** is a lead management system built for wedding venues and pros who want to stop losing inquiries and start booking more clients—automatically. From instant responses to automated follow-up and appointment scheduling, LeadLock helps you convert more leads with less stress. No more missed messages, no more disorganized inboxes—just a streamlined system that turns inquiries into “yes.”

Candidate B:
LeadLock is an inquiry management and follow-up system built for wedding venues and professionals. It helps turn more inquiries into booked tours, appointments, and clients—without relying on you to manage every follow-up manually.

From instant text and email responses to automated follow-up sequences, pipeline tracking, and appointment scheduling, LeadLock brings your inquiry process into one place. Built on the HighLevel platform with wedding-industry-specific strategy, templates, and workflows, it connects the interest your marketing creates with the conversations that lead to bookings.

Spend less time chasing inquiries and sorting through inboxes, and more time creating an exceptional experience for your couples—from their very first inquiry.
